title: Writing practice rubric
provenance: Written by EduWonderLab for classroom practice. Organized by the same three language dimensions WIDA uses (discourse, sentence, word/phrase) but it is NOT a WIDA rubric, uses none of its wording, and produces no WIDA score or level.

dimensions.label: Task completion
dimensions.look: Did the response do what the task asked, for the audience given?
descriptors: Little of the task is addressed.
Part of the task is addressed.
The main parts of the task are addressed.
The whole task is addressed, with purpose and audience clear.

dimensions.label: Organization
dimensions.look: Is there a clear beginning, middle and end, or a clear order of ideas?
descriptors: No clear order.
Some order, with gaps.
A clear order of ideas.
A clear order that guides the reader throughout.

dimensions.label: Development of ideas
dimensions.look: Are the ideas explained, not only listed?
descriptors: Ideas are listed or unclear.
Some ideas are explained.
Main ideas are explained.
Ideas are explained thoroughly and connected to the task.

dimensions.label: Vocabulary
dimensions.look: Are the words right for the topic?
descriptors: Few topic words.
Some topic words; some repeated or unclear.
Topic words are used and fit the meaning.
Precise topic and academic words are used.

dimensions.label: Language structures
dimensions.look: Do sentences carry the meaning, with some variety?
descriptors: Mostly fragments or single words.
Some complete sentences.
Complete sentences with some variety.
A variety of sentence types used with control.

dimensions.label: Cohesion
dimensions.look: Do connecting words and phrases link the ideas?
descriptors: Ideas are not linked.
A few linking words.
Linking words connect the main ideas.
Linking words and phrases connect ideas smoothly throughout.

dimensions.label: Evidence and elaboration
dimensions.look: Where the task needs it, does the writer use evidence from the text or data?
descriptors: No evidence is used.
Evidence is mentioned but not used.
Evidence supports the main points.
Specific evidence is used and explained.

dimensions.label: Clarity of meaning
dimensions.look: Can a reader understand the message?
descriptors: The message is very hard to understand.
The message is understood with effort.
The message is understood.
The message is easy to understand.

notScoredNote: The lab counts some features in the text (words, linking words, numbers used) as rule-based observations. It does not judge meaning and it does not score writing.
